result.rationale: The diff removes `afterModel` returning `model.findMembers()` promise and replaces it with fire-and-forget `model.findMembers()` inside `setupController` in both admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6. Also `findMembers` now returns undefined early for empty names (`return ;`). A rejected fetch is unhandled, so the members view silently renders empty, losing the transition-abort/error behavior the old code had. This is a real, verifiable error-visibility regression introduced by the diff.

judged_text: setupController fires model.findMembers() fire-and-forget with no rejection handler; the old afterModel returned the promise, so a fetch failure aborted the transition and surfaced, while the new code discards it. If the members fetch fails, the admin group page renders an empty member list with no error — indistinguishable from an empty group — a regression in error visibility for the admin members view.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the routes’ `afterModel` hooks that returned `model.findMembers()` (e.g. `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`) and replaces them with `setupController(...){ controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers(); }`, which does not return/chain the promise and has no rejection handling. Since `Discourse.Group#findMembers` performs `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` and no `.catch`, a request failure will no longer reject the transition or surface via the route hook; the page will render with `members` unset/empty (templates iterate `{{each ... in members}}`), making failures indistinguishable from an empty group. This is a real behavior regression introduced by the change.
